items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: After he left my band, he went a little while with Fletcher when Fletcher was on the road.

ctx.x: I don't know, Dick, but I assume that he is. After he left my band, he went a little while with Fletcher when Fletcher was on the road. He was always a fickle fellow, wanting a gold, gold, gold, so I imagine he just kept running. And I never heard from him, he's one of the characters that never did Carl Strawn much.
Yeah. But what did he do when the moon changed? Can you tell me?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: I believe he stayed with me longer than anyone he stayed with.

ctx.x: Well, you had Frank Jackay. Strictly a section man. Yeah. Geechee Robinson. Where did Frank Jackay come from? Lake Charles, Louisiana. Cousin to Illinois.
Who did he play with, Frank?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-12-30
items.q: And then when we went up a little further, when we added Geechee Robinson, another drum roll.

ctx.x: So you got a real close song, didn't you?

That was the first bass song. And then when we went up a little further, when we added Geechee Robinson, another drum roll. We had Nick Turner, another bass record. I had Jimmy Johnson on the string bass. And I had Nick Turner on the Suze for MWM on the drum roll. And then later on I added Harold Holmes, who's now in Canada, who did most of my arranging. And as we traveled over the country, I added here, subtracted, added and subtracted.
And I found the change in the years. Did you ever play any other state fairs? You want to start it by now or is it?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1974-01-01
items.q: in the band. They had names. Everyone had a nickname. For instance, I was twenty years old. I was the old man. And then of course, Geechee, I told you, he was right. And then, uh, Albert Martin was called Fats. And of course, Nicky got his name, Nicky.

ctx.x: Well, supposing some of the musicians would be talking about your coat or your tie. They'd say, watch it say the hawk's going to get it. They'd be having a cue to get hold of whatever it was, whoever the hawk was. I imagine somebody knew who the hawk was but they never knew. And then they used to call her, if a chick wasn't a nice looking chick, they would call her Taylor. And then she was not such a nice looking gal. What do you call her? Well, they call her a good looking chick. That's a nice looking Taylor.…
So, I guess, unless you can make something else, we'd better turn it up. We're almost to the end of the tape. Okay, thank you. Goodnight, Nicky. Goodnight.
